content_voiceover: This slide breaks down the QUAZAR overall survival benefit by how many consolidation cycles patients received before starting maintenance. Across all three subgroups, no consolidation, one consolidation, and two or more consolidations, oral azacitidine prolonged survival compared to placebo. Median overall survival ranged from twenty one to twenty eight point six months with oral azacitidine, versus only ten point nine to seventeen point six months with placebo. Interestingly, the hazard ratio was most favorable, zero point five five, in patients who received no consolidation at all, suggesting the benefit of maintenance is preserved or even more pronounced when consolidation chemotherapy was skipped or not tolerated. This is useful for boards because it shows the drug's benefit is consistent regardless of prior consolidation intensity.
keypoints: OS benefit with oral azacitidine held across all consolidation subgroups
No consolidation: HR zero point five five, most favorable
One consolidation: HR zero point seven five
Two or more consolidations: HR zero point seven five
keypoint_voiceover: Across consolidation subgroups from none to two or more cycles, oral azacitidine consistently prolonged survival versus placebo, with the strongest hazard ratio, zero point five five, seen in patients who had no consolidation at all.
